name: John of Salisbury
biography: Not an important original thinker but valuable as a witness to his times; secretary to three archbishops of Canterbury (including Becket); called himself an 'Academic' (skeptic) in matters outside the faith; admired Abelard but laughed at his and Roscelin's theories of universals; still regarded Plato as 'the prince of all philosophers.'
